title: Side setback, walls 3.6 m to 7 m high (R10-R25)
text: C3.4.1 Buildings are set back from lot boundaries in accordance with Table 3.4a. Refer Figure 3.4a, b, c. ii. For R10-R25, the stated setback distances may be reduced by half the width of an adjoining pedestrian access way to a maximum reduction of 2m (refer to Figure 3.4d). Table 3.4a Lot boundary setbacks, side setback: Wall height 3.6m to 7m 1.5m.

replaces.note: wall height and length matrix -> flat setback by wall height (C4P1-086)
major-opening setbacks (3.5 m to 5 m+) dropped
R10-R25 reduction by half an adjoining ROW, pedestrian access way, communal street or battleaxe leg -> pedestrian access way only (C4P1-089)

verified.note: 1.5m confirmed (Table 4A p7 agrees). Table 3.4a (p32) prints the bands as 'Wall height up to 3.5m', 'Wall height 3.6m to 7m' and 'Wall height above 7.1m', leaving 3.5-3.6 m and 7.0-7.1 m undefined; Table 4A (p7) prints '3.6m -7m (2nd storey)' and '7.1m and above (3rd storey)'. The encoded band conditions (> 3.5, > 7.0) are an inference.

notes: from: ch3 C3.4.1#side-3.6-to-7m. Table 3.4a (p32) side setback 1.5 m, the same at every code; C3.4.1(ii) (pedestrian access way, half its width, max 2 m) is limited to R10-R25, so this band carries it as an exception and R30-R60 is a separate rule. No length or major-opening distinction (C4P1-086). Rounding gap between wall-height bands (3.5-3.6 m, 7.0-7.1 m) unresolved. Applies only where the building has walls 3.6 m to 7 m high (condition on building.has_walls_3_6_to_7m); the band does not depend on the building's maximum wall height.
